title: Bellarmine is wrong: many heretics sold unwritten tradition — Irenaeus and Jerome say so
source_text: XXIV. Deinde falsum est quod sumit Bellarminus, nempe, haereticos omnes traditiones rejecisse. Nam fuerunt quidem haeretici nonnulli qui traditiones non scriptas contempserunt, & soli Scripturae sese inhaerere profitebantur, quamvis varie illam corrumperent; sed fuerunt quoque multi haeretici qui traditiones quasdam non scriptas venditabant, & eo fuco atque colore utebantur, ut figmenta & somnia sua apud populum commendarent. Id docet Irenaeus lib. 3. c. 2. Haeretici, inquit, resistunt & repugnant saluti suae: quum enim ex Scripturis arguuntur, in accusationem convertuntur ipsarum Scripturarum, quasi non recte habeant, neque sint ex authoritate, & quia varie sint dictae, & quia non possit ex his inveniri veritas ab his qui nesciant traditionem; non enim per literas traditam illam, sed per vivam vocem. Imo haeretici illi, quos hoc in loco perstringit Irenaeus, sunt ipsi Marcionitae, & Valentiniani, aliique similes, quos tanquam traditionum hostes producit Bellarminus. Quibus consona docet Hieronymus commentar. in Aggaeum, De haereticis enim loquens, Quae, inquit, absque authoritate & testimoniis Scripturarum, quasi traditione Apostolica sponte reperiunt & confingunt, percutit gladius Dei. Et supra retulimus Augustini verba, quibus testatur veteres haereticos abusos fuisse, ad traditiones suas confirmandas, illis ipsis Christi verbis, quibus Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae simili modo hodie abutuntur, nempe, Adhuc habeo multa vobis dicere, sed non potestis portare modo.
pass_a_gloss: Next, what Bellarmine assumes is false, namely that all heretics rejected traditions. For there were indeed some heretics who despised unwritten traditions and professed to cling to Scripture alone, though they corrupted it in various ways; but there were also many heretics who hawked certain unwritten traditions, and used that varnish and color to commend their figments and dreams to the people. Irenaeus teaches this in book 3 chapter 2. Heretics, he says, resist and fight against their own salvation: for when they are argued from the Scriptures, they turn to an accusation of the Scriptures themselves, as if they were not right, nor of authority, and because they are said variously, and because the truth cannot be found from them by those who do not know tradition; for it was not handed down through letters, but through living voice. Nay those heretics whom Irenaeus strikes in this place are the Marcionites themselves, and the Valentinians, and others like them, whom Bellarmine produces as enemies of traditions. Jerome teaches in harmony in the commentary on Haggai, speaking of heretics: Those things, he says, which without the authority and testimonies of the Scriptures they spontaneously invent and feign as if by Apostolic tradition, the sword of God strikes. And above we reported Augustine's words, by which he testifies that the ancient heretics abused, to confirm their traditions, those very words of Christ which the Doctors of the Roman Church abuse in a similar way today, namely, I still have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now.
pass_b_english: Bellarmine's premise fails: not every heretic dumped tradition.
Some sneered at unwritten tradition while twisting Scripture; many others sold oral tradition as cover for figments.
Irenaeus: the Marcionites and Valentinians — Bellarmine's alleged tradition-foes — fled Scripture for living-voice tradition.
Jerome and Augustine: heretics forge apostolic tradition and abuse John 16 the same way Rome does now.
